title: Maple Aisle retail integration capture
content:
Call notes + integration sketch (Maple Aisle)

Attendees: Priya (Redwood CS), Liam (Redwood SE), Sara (Maple Aisle Eng), Daniel (Maple Aisle PM)
Date: 2025-02-11
Context: Retail chain (450 stores, hybrid cloud + small on-prem edge boxes in stores). Pilot: product recommender + returns triage chat widget. Goal: reduce returns processing time and improve in-store associate answer quality without touching PII.

Key constraints / facts from call:
- On-prem edge boxes: 2x A100-equivalent in ~200 stores (pilot group), older T4s in rest. Network out is constrained (700ms RTT to cloud in some regions).
- Data flow: POS events are sensitive; Maple Aisle wants only product metadata (non-PII) to go to hosted endpoints. Customer can run Redwood Private for PII lane, or route obfuscated payloads to hosted.
- SLA target for in-store assistant: 95th percentile < 350ms token-latency end-to-end when served from edge; acceptable fallback to hosted with degraded latency (1.2–2s) for non-critical queries.
- Token budget per query target: ~1200 tokens (including prompt + generation). Cost sensitivity: want to keep per-interaction token cost low for scale (estimate 3M interactions/mo at pilot scale).
- Security: Must integrate with their KMS for keys, and audit logs required for all customer-visible responses.

Integration gotchas / concerns called out:
1) Tokenization mismatch: their product SKU descriptions contain lots of short codes and slash-separated tokens. Need to validate tokenizer behavior for the candidate model or run small eval. Possible pre-processing step: expand slashes, normalize SKUs before embedding.
2) Prefix cache effectiveness: many queries start with same store-specific prefixes (store hours, local promos). We should instrument prefix hit rate in early pilot to tune cache TTLs and shard assignment.
3) Edge model variants: their T4s can't run FP16 70B comfortably; propose quantized 13B family on-store (int8/4) and keep 70B for central host. Need to test quality delta for recommendation prompts.
4) Network partition fallback: if store loses connection to central control plane, local assistant must continue using pinned model and local config; will need a lightweight policy in the agent.
5) PII redaction: returns descriptions sometimes include customer names typed by associates. Recommend local pre-run redaction rules before sending to hosted endpoints; document false-positive/negative risk and logging behavior.

Immediate technical notes / sketches (Liam):
- Local runtime: run Redwood Private runtime packaged container on-store. Use model variant file: rwd-13b-quant-v1. Shard rule: pinned to local pod, use local KV cache for repeated prefix prompts.
- API surface: minimal forwarder: /v1/generate with headers X-Store-ID, X-Assoc-ID (hashed), X-Model-Variant. Add preference header Accept-Fallback: hosted|local
- Observability: emit token-level counters to central metrics when online; buffer and forward on reconnect. Add healthcheck endpoint for canary automation.
- Example sample request (to test during bench): {"prompt":"Find complementary items for SKU: G-4932/XL","max_tokens":"120","store_id":"s-204"}
- Bench targets: on T4: p50 gen latency < 220ms for 256-token generation; p95 < 600ms. On A100-equivalent p95 < 350ms.

Quality evaluation plan:
- Create 250 prompt pairs from their historical cart + returns logs (redacted) to compare 13B quant vs hosted 70B. Metrics: relevance@k, factual accuracy (manual label), hallucination rate, BLEU-ish free-text overlap for recommended SKUs.
- Acceptance threshold: 13B quant must hit >= 85% of 70B relevance score and hallucination delta < 5%. If below, propose hybrid routing (short queries local, long/complex routed to hosted 70B).

Rollout / rollout policy idea (Daniel):
- Week 0–2: bench + QA on 5 pilot stores (T4 and A100 mix), run automated traffic simulation.
- Week 3–4: 50-store pilot with canary rollout: 5% traffic to new heuristic, 25% after verified; automatic rollback on error rate > 2% or latency SLO breach.
- Canary config: model variant tags, routing policy, cache TTLs. Use Redwood Console to create a canary route and add tracing for affected store IDs.

Action items (owners + target dates):
- Priya: Draft compliance checklist for PII handling and redaction rules; share with Maple legal. Due: 2025-02-14.
- Liam: Spin up bench harness (docker-compose + sample store data) and run quantized 13B baseline on T4. Capture p50/p95. Due: 2025-02-18.
- Sara: Share 500 redacted return transcripts and product description CSV (SKU, short_desc, long_desc). Note: scrub PII before upload. Due: 2025-02-13.
- Daniel: Confirm which stores will be in initial pilot and provide network perf stats for those locations (RTT, bandwidth). Due: 2025-02-12.
- Maya: Create Redwood Console dashboard template for store-level latency and prefix cache hit rate. Due: 2025-02-20.

Open questions to resolve (for next sync):
- Can Maple Aisle accept a transient increase in latency for complex queries routed to hosted? (Daniel to confirm business tolerance)
- What exact KMS provider and key rotation cadence? We need KMS customer admin contact.
- Are returns notes stored in their data lake with PII redaction metadata? If not, we need process/contract to handle removal.

Notes to self (quick):
- Run small tokenizer probe on 50 SKU examples ASAP; add to bench harness.
- Suggest trying both rwd-13b-quant-v1 and rwd-7b-q2 to evaluate cost-quality tradeoffs.
- Keep an eye on KV cache sizing; store-specific prefixes mean heavy reuse but different vocab per store.

Next meeting: 2025-02-18 11:00 PT (tentative) - technical deep-dive with Maple eng for bench results and initial canary config.

Random brainstorm (low priority):
- Local personalization: keep store-level small embedding index for trending SKUs; run cheap recall locally and only consult hosted model for edge-case disambiguation.
- Assistant UI: include a confidence score and an easy "ask HQ" toggle that forces hosted path and logs for manual review.

End of capture.
